Le Beroë globuleux. ( Medusa pileus.)
grouped under Beroe, perhaps as a subgenus? with text
Müller and Bruguières separate from the jellyfish.
THE BEROE. (BEROE.)
Which have a gelatinous body, of oval shape, divided by furrows
into ribs, like a melon. At one of the extremities is an
opening that serves as a mouth, from which, in some species,
two more or less long and divided tentacles emerge. The ribs
are ciliated. They use these cilia to propel themselves through
the water, swimming in a rotating motion. They are
phosphorescent and emit a bright glow at night.
subject: pileus_müller.o.f_1776
